title: Inventory management
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers inventory management or stock valuation methods like FIFO and LIFO; the closest, on resources needed to start, only mentions planning stock before opening.

draft.title: Inventory management
card: Inventory is the stock a business holds, such as materials, partly finished goods and finished goods. Holding enough stock means the business does not run out and lose sales or stop production.
Holding stock has costs. The business pays for storage space, insurance and handling, and its money is tied up in goods that are not yet sold. Stock can also be damaged, stolen or go out of date.
first in, first out. It assumes the oldest stock is used or sold first, so the stock left over is valued at the newest prices.
last in, first out. It assumes the newest stock is used or sold first, so the stock left over is valued at the oldest prices.
draft.remember: Stock protects against running out but costs money to hold. FIFO and LIFO are two ways to value it.

a.q: Which is a cost of holding a large amount of inventory?
opts: Money is tied up in unsold goods
The business may run out of stock
Stock is valued at the newest prices
The oldest stock is always sold first
a.why: Unsold stock holds money that the business could use elsewhere. Running out of stock is the risk of holding too little, not a cost of holding a lot.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the money spent on the stock.

b.q: Dev's hardware store in Bathurst bought 100 drills at $40, then 100 at $50. It sells 100 drills. Under FIFO, how are the 100 drills left in stock valued?
opts: At $50 each, the price of the newest stock
At $40 each, the price of the oldest stock
At $45 each, the average of the two prices
At $50 each, because the newest was sold first
b.why: FIFO assumes the oldest drills, bought at $40, were sold first. The drills left are the newer ones, so they are valued at $50. The $40 option describes LIFO, where the oldest stock is left.
b.clue: FIFO sells the oldest first, so which stock remains?

a.best: Money is tied up in unsold goods

b.best: At $50 each, the price of the newest stock
